response.rationale: R1 best explains the odontogenic maxillary presentation: maxillary ridge expansion with primary tooth mobility, painless bony-hard swelling, and a well-circumscribed expansile mixed-density maxillary mass with aggressive local invasion. R2 captures the destructive sinonasal/pterygopalatine pattern but lacks the odontogenic/tooth-mobility signature and classic epistaxis/nasal obstruction; R4 and R3 are excluded by destructive multi-space involvement and unilaterality.

rejected.why: Fibrous dysplasia would produce ground-glass remodeling rather than destructive perforation of nasal septum, sphenoid, pterygoid plates, and infraorbital rim; also lacks the tooth-mobility signature.
Cherubism is bilateral/symmetric, familial, and mandible-predominant; this is a unilateral maxillary destructive mass with no family history.
